threads.title: Siblings caring for aging dad can't meet in person or electronically. Text threads get way too long for effective communication. What to do?
hits: I love CaringBridge but it's basically no different that us communicating here on this forum. Zoom would be the best option. Not everyone has experience typing fast like me so they'd hate all the typing. Someone mentioned FaceTime but I don't think you can have more than 2 person at a time.

threads.title: Does anyone use a symptoms sheet or flow chart so multiple caregivers (family) stay in the loop?
hits: There's a free website called Caring Bridge (caringbridgedotorg) that enables you to email multiple family members and keep everyone up-to-date. I'm not sure what all of the features of the website include, but you might start there.

threads.title: What is the name of the service that allows you to posts daily updates of loved ones condition?
hits: Caringbridge website - you can create a personal site with health info that people can become members of. I don't think it costs anything - several cancer patients that I know have used it to communicate with family that does not have Facebook.

threads.title: Emergency alert, necklace recommendations
hits: We used Great Call Lively for my dad with great success. They had a list in descending order of who to call when he fell. They first confirmed the fall with him, asked he needed emergency services called, then called relatives in order given for help to come. They were good about setting it up according to our wishes. It was dependent on him wearing it and him having a sound mind, it wouldn’t have worked without it

threads.title: What’s the best medical alert device to keep my mom safe?
hits: We used Great Call, which is now Lively, with my dad and had success for the most part. He cooperated with wearing the pendant , it detected falls and he pushed the button sometimes when he needed help. The operator asked him who he wanted called from 911 to a list of relatives. I will add, the one time he fell and was on the floor for over 12 hours, the pendant was on the charger, so useless. Dad didn’t have any dementia which helped with cooperation and remembering to use it most all the time

threads.title: Has anyone had experience with the cell phone Jitterbug?
hits: My dad has had two of the Jitterbug phones and the emergency service you can get with it. We never had any problem with the phone and when we had any questions about it (like when he let it run out of battery for so long that I thought it was broken when it was taking so long to recharge) they were very helpful at troubleshooting and getting it fixed. Also he never had to use the emergency service but he did press the emergency button often just to "test it". He liked knowing that they could identify where he was when he was not actually at home. The always answered promptly and asked "Is this an emergency?" He would say "no, just testing" and then they would confirm his name, current location, and ask if there was anything that they could do for him. I was very impressed with the operators. I've recommended it to many people. I think it is a great service not only for the elderly but for people with small children who may have a cell phone for emergency purposes. If a child was frightened walking home from school pushing 1 emergency button is lots easier to remember than mom's phone number.

threads.title: Fall detection medical alert device.
hits: We signed Mom up for Medical Guardian, specifically for the fall detection. She has fallen five or six times without it alerting, and alerted one time when she hadn't fallen. I'm in contact with customer service, but has anyone else had this issues, specifically with this company?

threads.title: I'm in search for a medical alert system that would contact me and other family members that won't have monthly fees and isn't costly. Any suggestions?
hits: We got our mother a system from Medical Guardian- $400 per year, no monthly charges and you can program it to do what you need. I am in Massachusetts. Not sure what is available in your area.

threads.title: Doctor's office won't answer a question via the patient portal without appointment.
hits: About 2 weeks after seeing a neurologist, I, the invoked health care proxy, sent a question via the patient portal regarding questions related to the appointment. The front desk staff demanded we set up another appointment with the aging parent to get the question(s) answered.
